content.body:
The Vickers Mark VI actually formed a large bulk of Britain's tank forces at the outset of the war. It was intended to be deployed as a reconnaissance vehicle and mainly for colonial low-intensity conflicts. Meant for infantry support only, their light armor could not withstand even close AP machinegun fire. Many were thrust into the role of light battle tank with predictably high casualties. Note that the .50 caliber machinegun is not the impressive M2 .50 cal later brought into the war by the Americans, but simply a gun with similar .50 caliber bullets but with much poorer performance.
The Vickers is a nimble, quick vehicle which can maintain a high speed even off-road. Its green coloring makes it hard to spot in any sort of broken brush or against a tree-line. The question is why would you want to go into battle with a Vicky? There are very few strong points about this tank. The concentrated MG fire can provide a modicum of self-propelled anti-aircraft capability to an infantry assault, but the fountain of tracer fire will attract ATR soldiers, rifle grenadiers, and light tanks to your position like vultures to road kill.
However, it can provide some support for AT guns or other weapons that need to keep away the infantry, especially using the commander's optics to search for enemies.
The .50 cal is not particularly accurate, so even moderate range fire requires long bursts to be effective. While it has trouble protecting itself from virtually any form of attack from an armored vehicle, it is useful as a source of suppressive firepower for attacking infantry. The numbers present in the BEF battle order made it logically necessary for the Vickers to be included in the game, but it will almost certainly be your last choice as an armored vehicle to take on any mission.
Control Variations: The driver may zoom his view through an open view slit (numpad . or Del key). When the view slit is closed, he cannot see outside at all. The main gun of the Vickers is the .50 caliber MG with a co-axial .303 MG.
